messages:
sarah-support: FYI customer reported big latency + increased token charges. They say requests are going to EU and timing out from their US infra. They include examples.

tom-customer: We saw 500ms -> 1500ms after last week. No code changes on our side. SDK v0.9.2.

sarah-support: Repro steps they gave:
```
curl -v \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx" \
  -H "X-Client-Region: eu-west" \
  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate?region=us-east" \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}'
```
They claim query param region=us-east but header X-Client-Region set by their proxy to eu-west.

alex-eng-runtime: Pinged — on our side routing precedence was historically: header X-Region/X-Client-Region -> query param -> auth claim. That matches these logs: `routed_to: eu-west (reason: X-Client-Region)` so header wins. Was there expectation otherwise?

tom-customer: We assumed region query param should override proxy-inserted header. Our stack inserts header upstream and we can't easily remove it. We thought SDK param would be authoritative.

lee-qa: I can repro locally: when both present, header takes precedence. Quick test:
```
> curl -H 'X-Client-Region: eu-west' 'https://api.redwood.example/v1/health?region=us-east'
{ "region": "eu-west", "latency_ms": 1200 }
```

sarah-support: This is causing customer latency and also billing to the wrong capacity pool. They want guidance + timeline to fix.

alex-eng-runtime: Checking recent commits — looks like a routing refactor in Feb flipped precedence to header-first to handle some edge cases (internal services). We didn't document that change. Not ideal.

maria-eng-platform: We need to decide desired precedence. Our public API docs say query param or SDK config should be the client control. Internal headers should be treated as lower trust unless they come from our trusted gateways. Proposal: trust explicit param > sdk config > header, unless header is from internal gateway (we can verify via X-Forwarded-For + cert).

alex-eng-runtime: Agree. I'll prepare a small runtime patch to prefer explicit query param over X-Client-Region and add a quick config switch to drop untrusted region headers.

lee-qa: Test plan: unit tests + e2e with proxy that injects header. Will verify routing, auth, and fallback behavior.

sarah-support: Interim mitigations for customer: 1) set header X-Client-Region to us-east (if they can modify proxy), or 2) send region via Authorization metadata claim (we can accept `region` in bearer metadata), or 3) upgrade to patched SDK once available. Which is quickest?

tom-customer: We can temporarily set X-Client-Region: us-east on our proxy. Do you confirm that will route to US?

alex-eng-runtime: Yes, setting header to us-east will force US routing right now. But we don't recommend that permanently. We'll push a config change to prefer query param within 3 business days and a runtime patch in the next release cycle.

maria-eng-platform: I'll also add a feature-flag to drop untrusted region headers by default for hosted customers and add telemetry to catch these conflicts.

deploy-bot: Canary: Routing-config-change v2.1 -> us-east cluster started (canary 5%) at 2026-03-12T14:05:00Z.

alex-eng-runtime: Patch ready, ran local tests. Need ops deploy window. I think we can do canary today and full roll tomorrow if no regressions.

sarah-support: Sent customer instructions to set header to us-east as temporary workaround and informed them about the upcoming fix.

tom-customer: Applied header override. Confirming latency back to ~120ms, tokens billed to US pool. Thanks. :relieved:

lee-qa: Ran integration tests against canary — header vs param precedence now respects query param override. No failures in 2000 runs.

maria-eng-platform: Config flag rolled to 100% for hosted routing; added telemetry alert for conflicted region signals.

alex-eng-runtime: Deployed runtime patch in next release (v0.9.4) to make precedence explicit and to log conflict warnings.

sarah-support: Customer verified normal behavior and billing. Closing on our side but leaving docs update task open: update region routing docs and SDK release notes.

lee-qa: Filed test-case #RT-482: region-header-conflict.
